ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Between the parallel lines MN, PQ, and MP (including the boundaries), there is a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the plane of the paper, with a magnetic induction strength of $B$. The angle between the boundaries MN and MP is $\alpha = 30^\circ$. At point P, there is an ion source that can emit positive and negative ions of various speeds into the magnetic field region. The ions are emitted in a direction parallel to the plane of the paper and perpendicular to MP. After moving for some time, the ions can exit the magnetic field from different boundaries. It is known that for ions exiting from boundary PQ, the ion with the maximum distance between the exit point and point P has a velocity of $v_0$. The charge-to-mass ratio $k$ is the same for all positive and negative ions. The effects of gravity and interactions between ions are negligible.

1. Find the length of MP; do not add any other content.
2. Find the maximum velocity of ions emitted from the boundary MP.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two horizontal dashed boundary lines, the upper one is MN, and the lower one is PQ, the two are parallel; on the left side there is a dashed boundary MP from M slanting down to the right to P. The magnetic field region is inside the region enclosed by these boundaries, using dotted symbols to indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the paper surface outward, marked with B. In the figure, at M, the angle between MP and the horizontal boundary MN is marked as \alpha=30^\circ; point P is located on the lower boundary PQ, and the velocity arrow near point P indicates that the ion is emitted from P, in the direction perpendicular to MP. Reasoning: Let P be the origin, PQ be the positive x-axis, and MN be y=H. Let the length of MP be L. From the geometric relation in the image, the angle between MP and the horizontal boundary is 30^\circ, so the distance between the two parallel boundaries H=L\sin30^\circ=L/2. The ion undergoes circular motion in the uniform magnetic field, with radius r=v/(kB). For the charge sign that can be emitted from the PQ boundary, the center of the circle is at the lower right of P, and its coordinates can be written as (\sqrt{3}r/2,-r/2). When this circle intersects PQ again, the distance from the intersection point to P is \sqrt{3}r, therefore the distance from the exit point on PQ to P increases as r increases. In order still to be emitted from PQ, the highest point of the circular arc cannot exceed the upper boundary MN; the height of the highest point of this circle is r/2, so the maximum case satisfies r/2=H=L/2, giving r=L. The problem states that the ion emitted from PQ and whose exit point is farthest from P has speed v_0, therefore L=r=v_0/(kB). For the opposite charge sign, the center of the circle is on MP and its vertical height relative to P is r/2. The highest point of this circular arc before returning to MP has height 3r/2. If it is to be emitted from the MP boundary without first touching MN, there should be 3r/2\le H=L/2, so r\le L/3. Therefore the maximum speed emitted from the MP boundary is v_{\max}=kB(L/3)=v_0/3.
